transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Gotcha, if she’s catching calls, that’s working for you right now. Mhm, when she steps away—lunch, sick days, after hours—what happens to calls that come in then?
User: We just call people back when she returns. We've never really counted how many calls we miss though.
Agent: Got it, so you’re calling back once she’s free, you just don’t know how many slip through. Roughly how many calls a week would you guess are going to voicemail or ringing out before she can grab them?
User: We don't really track that, but it's not like we're missing a ton. Maybe a handful here and there.
Agent: Makes sense, if it’s just a handful here and there it doesn’t feel urgent. When someone does hit voicemail or can’t get through, do they usually leave a message or do you think some just call the next place?
User: Some leave a message, but I'm sure a few might try another shop if they don't get through.
Agent: Yeah, that’s what I hear a lot—some wait, some just move on. If one of those “handful” of missed calls is, say, a $600–$1,000 job, would you want a way to have every one of those callers actually booked or at least texted back in real time instead of hoping they call again?
User: Sounds like a solution looking for a problem. We've been doing fine without extra layers so far.
Agent: Totally hear you—if it feels like a “nice to have,” it’s not worth adding more stuff. Just so I don’t keep pushing something you don’t need, what would actually have to break or change with your phones for you to say, “yeah, we should look at something different”?
User: If we started missing more calls consistently and it hurt our bookings, then maybe I'd reconsider.
Agent: That makes sense—you don’t fix what isn’t clearly broken. So for you, it really comes down to bookings; do you have a target number of new jobs or dollar amount you’re aiming to add each month, or are you mostly focused on just keeping things steady right now?
User: We focus on keeping things steady. No specific target, just maintaining our usual flow of work.
Agent: Gotcha, so as long as the work keeps flowing, you’re good. Out of curiosity, if I could show you a way to keep your current setup but automatically catch those “handful” of missed callers and turn even one or two a month into booked jobs, would that be worth a 10–15 minute look with Jay just to see if the numbers make sense, or would you rather leave things as-is for now?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Book your demo.
Agent: Nice, that makes a lot of sense as a backup. When during the week is usually better for you to talk with Jay for 10–15 minutes—earlier in the week or closer to the end?
User: Earlier in the week works for me. Send over the details, and we'll set something up.
Agent: Got it, we’ll line something up for early in the week and send over the details so you can lock in a time that works. Before I do that, do you prefer mornings or afternoons for a quick 10–15 minute call with Jay?
User: Mornings usually work best for me. Just let me know the time, and I'll make it work.
Agent: Perfect, mornings it is. What’s your email so we can send over a couple of early‑week morning options with Jay for a 20‑minute, no‑commitment walkthrough?
User: Email me at dave@kowalskiautobody.com with the details, and I'll look out for it.
Agent: Sounds good, Dave — we’ll email those early‑week morning options to you at that address so you can pick what works best, and that’ll lock in your walkthrough with Jay. Really appreciate you being open to a backup layer for those missed calls; anything else you’d like to cover before we wrap up today?
